title: Azure.Security.KeyVault.Secrets
description: Securely store and retrieve secrets, keys, and certificates from Azure Key Vault.

data.text: This package lets you read and write secrets from Azure Key Vault. It uses `Azure.Identity` for authentication and provides a simple API for managing application secrets.
Create a `SecretClient` using your vault URI and a credential from `Azure.Identity`.

data.title: Set and Get Secrets
Key Vault Terms
items: Vault — a secure storage container for secrets, keys, and certificates.
Secret — a string value (e.g., a password or API key).
Key Vault URI — the HTTPS endpoint of your vault, e.g., `https://myvault.vault.azure.net/`.

terms.definition: The main client for reading and writing secrets in Key Vault.
Represents a secret including its name, value, and metadata.
A Key Vault feature that lets you recover deleted secrets.

data.title: Security Note
data.text: Key Vault access should be restricted via Azure RBAC or Key Vault access policies.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `SecretClient` to manage secrets in Key Vault.
Authenticate with `DefaultAzureCredential` for the best developer experience.
Never store secrets in appsettings.json or source control.
data.takeaway: Azure Key Vault keeps sensitive configuration out of your code and configuration files.

data.title: Exercise: Store and Retrieve a Secret
data.description: Create a console app that stores a connection string in Key Vault and retrieves it on startup.
steps: Retrieve and print the secret value.
data.expectedOutcome: You can securely manage secrets in Azure Key Vault from a .NET app.
